section: Video diffusion models against NeuWorld on test scenes

inputs.neuworld: the scene graph (objects, properties, joints, start state) and the action; no image and no text
inputs.video_models: the rendered first frame and a text prompt that describes the scene, the action and, in order, the outcome

tile_note: Every tile of a record shows the same crop of the same camera for the same number of seconds. The video models generate 16 frames a second (5.1 s for Wan2.2, 5.8 s for Cosmos-Predict2.5); they are shown at their own clock, cut to the length of the PhysX clip. Cosmos-Predict2.5 writes 1280 x 704, stretched back to 16:9.
selection_note: Records picked by hand from the 41 test records of the video-model study (one per motion family), where NeuWorld is close to PhysX and the motion is easy to see. They are examples, not a sample; the table reports all scorable records.

table.caption: Video models (outcome prompt) and the three NeuWorld variants on 36 test scenes, each from a different motion family (the video-model table of the supplementary, Sec. G.1). Error: position error in metres of the tracked objects over the first 5 s. Pace and direction are 1 when the objects move at the true speed and in the true direction. Time: one clip on one GPU.
table.source: tables/video_models.tex of the paper; measured on the clips generated from the darker first frames, not on the clips shown on the page

items.description: A spring plunger shoots a metal ball into a tower of blocks; the tower collapses and the blocks scatter.
items.neuworld_note: The tower collapses and the blocks scatter in the same directions as in PhysX; single blocks end in different places.
items.video_model_note: In Wan2.2 a coiled rod extends from the launcher and many additional blocks appear on the floor; in Cosmos-Predict2.5 the tower turns into a heap with many additional blocks.

tiles.label: Wan2.2 I2V-A14B
tiles.prompt: A video from a fixed camera showing a 3D-rendered empty room with a dark wooden floor. An orange robot arm holds back a spring plunger behind a metal ball on the floor. A tower of stacked blocks stands to the right of the ball. The arm lets go of the plunger. The plunger shoots the ball into the tower. The tower collapses, blocks scatter to the right and toward the camera, and the ball rolls on among them. The camera is fixed and captures the complete motion. The objects stay rigid.

items.description: An arm pulls the pin of a catapult; the beam swings up to nearly vertical and flings a ball into the air.
items.neuworld_note: The beam swings up and throws the ball, as in PhysX.
items.video_model_note: In Wan2.2 the arm lifts the whole beam off its post; in Cosmos-Predict2.5 the beam stays down for three seconds and is then carried away by the arm.

tiles.label: Wan2.2 I2V-A14B
tiles.prompt: A video from a fixed camera showing a 3D-rendered furnished room with a dark wooden floor. A long blue catapult beam is tilted on a dark post, with a black ball in its low end near the floor. An orange robot arm stands behind the beam. The arm pulls out the pin holding the beam. The beam swings up to nearly vertical and flings the ball into the air. The ball lands behind the beam and rolls away toward the back wall. The camera is fixed and captures the complete motion. The background furniture stays still. The objects stay rigid.

items.description: An arm pushes a ball across a table; the ball knocks a block off the edge into a box and follows it in.
items.neuworld_note: The block and the ball both land in the box within the first second and a half, as in PhysX.
items.video_model_note: In both video models the ball and the block stay on the table for two to three seconds before anything falls; in Wan2.2 only the ball ends in the box.

The ball knocks the block off the edge into the box, then rolls off after it and also lands in the box. The camera is fixed and captures the complete motion. The background furniture stays still. The objects stay rigid.

items.description: An arm pushes a ball into a tight cluster of six balls, which breaks apart.
items.neuworld_note: The cluster breaks apart and most balls roll out in the same directions as in PhysX.
items.video_model_note: In both video models additional balls appear: the seven balls become dozens.

tiles.label: Wan2.2 I2V-A14B
tiles.prompt: A video from a fixed camera showing a 3D-rendered empty room with a dark wooden floor. An orange robot arm stands next to a dark ball on the floor. A tight cluster of six more balls, mostly blue, lies just in front of it. The arm pushes the dark ball into the cluster. The cluster breaks apart. The balls roll away in different directions across the floor, several toward the camera, and they keep rolling steadily. The camera is fixed and captures the complete motion. The objects stay rigid.

items.description: An arm pulls a support block out from under two piles of blocks that carry a beam; the piles collapse.
items.neuworld_note: The piles collapse and the beam drops as in PhysX; the fallen blocks stay closer to the base than in PhysX.
items.video_model_note: In Wan2.2 the arm swings up and lifts the top of the pile; in Cosmos-Predict2.5 the pile turns into a heap with additional blocks.
items.in_paper: Fig. 8 of the supplementary (shown there with NeuWorld+FM)

tiles.label: Wan2.2 I2V-A14B
tiles.prompt: A video from a fixed camera showing a 3D-rendered furnished room with a dark wooden floor. Two tall piles of stacked dark and blue blocks stand on a dark base with a wide beam across their tops. An orange robot arm grips a support block at the bottom. The arm pulls the support block out. The piles collapse. The beam drops and lands tilted on the fallen blocks, and the blue blocks slide far across the floor to the right. The camera is fixed and captures the complete motion. The background furniture stays still. The objects stay rigid.

items.description: A pendulum swings into a tower of blocks and knocks its top layer to the floor; the rest of the tower stays standing.
items.neuworld_note: Only the top layer is knocked off, as in PhysX.
items.video_model_note: In Wan2.2 the whole tower falls into a heap; in Cosmos-Predict2.5 the tower grows to about twice its height, the ball stops at its top and no block falls.

tiles.label: Wan2.2 I2V-A14B
tiles.prompt: A video from a fixed camera showing a 3D-rendered furnished room with a dark wooden floor. A metal ball on a long thin rod hangs from a dark post, held out to one side. A tower of stacked blocks stands on the floor below. The ball is released and swings down. The ball hits the tower's top layer. All three of its blocks fall to the floor, the rest of the tower keeps standing, and the ball swings on. The camera is fixed and captures the complete motion. The background furniture stays still. The objects stay rigid.

items.description: An arm lets go of a ball at the top of a ramp; it hits a spring-mounted block, which topples a row of tall blocks one after another.
items.neuworld_note: The row falls in order, as in PhysX.
items.video_model_note: In Wan2.2 the ball reaches the row after about three seconds, then a coil spring with a block on top appears and the tiles lie scattered on the floor; in Cosmos-Predict2.5 more tiles appear in the row, the ball rolls past it and no tile falls.

tiles.label: Wan2.2 I2V-A14B
tiles.prompt: A video from a fixed camera showing a 3D-rendered empty room with a dark wooden floor. An orange robot arm holds a ball at the top of a wide brown ramp. At its foot stand a spring-mounted block and a row of tall thin blocks on end. The arm lets go of the ball. The ball rolls down and hits the spring-mounted block, which moves into the row. The blocks fall one after another and all end on the floor. The camera is fixed and captures the complete motion. The objects stay rigid.

items.description: An arm drops a large ball into a net of tiles held by springs; the net stretches down and the ball settles in the dip.
items.neuworld_note: The ball drops in, the net sags and the ball settles, as in PhysX.
items.video_model_note: In Wan2.2 the net turns into a wire basket and the tiles spread over the floor; in Cosmos-Predict2.5 the arm lowers the ball onto the net and keeps holding it, and the net does not stretch.

tiles.label: Wan2.2 I2V-A14B
tiles.prompt: A video from a fixed camera showing a 3D-rendered furnished room with a dark wooden floor. An orange robot arm holds a large orange ball high above a net of small blue and orange tiles stretched across a dark table-like frame. The arm lets go of the ball. The ball drops into the net, which stretches far down. The ball bounces up a little, drops in again and settles in the dip while the tiles keep swaying. The camera is fixed and captures the complete motion. The background furniture stays still.

items.description: An arm pushes a block into a ball; the block stops and the ball rolls away fast toward the camera.
items.neuworld_note: The block stops and the ball rolls toward the camera, more slowly than in PhysX.
items.video_model_note: In Wan2.2 the block travels across the floor together with the ball; in Cosmos-Predict2.5 the view moves closer while the block and the ball stay in place.

tiles.label: Wan2.2 I2V-A14B

An orange robot arm stands behind an upright blue block on the floor, with a metal ball just in front of the block. The arm pushes the block into the ball. The block stops after the impact, and the ball rolls away fast toward the camera until it leaves the picture. The camera is fixed and captures the complete motion. The objects stay rigid.
